title: The Lord’s Supper
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Lord’s Supper is the church’s commanded remembrance and proclamation of Christ’s saving death until He comes. In it, believers remember, give thanks, examine themselves, and share fellowship around the body and blood of Christ.
summary: The Lord’s Supper is the church’s commanded remembrance and proclamation of Christ’s saving death until He comes. In it, believers remember, give thanks, examine themselves, and share fellowship around the body and blood of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gave the Supper to His church as a sign of His body given and His blood poured out. The Supper points believers back to the cross and forward to His return.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Lord’s Supper was instituted by Jesus on the night He was betrayed. The bread and cup point to His body given and His blood of the covenant poured out for many.

The Supper is an act of remembrance and proclamation. The church declares the Lord’s death until He comes, keeping the cross at the center of its gathered life.

The Supper also calls for examination. Believers should not treat holy things casually or selfishly. The church must approach the table with faith, repentance, love, and discernment.

The Lord’s Supper strengthens fellowship. The one bread points to the one body. Believers come not as isolated individuals, but as Christ’s people receiving the sign of His saving death together.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
The church can drift from the cross even while staying busy. The Lord’s Supper brings believers repeatedly back to Christ’s body and blood.

This doctrine also teaches reverence and hope. The table is not empty ritual, but a serious, grace-filled remembrance of Christ’s sacrifice and a preview of the coming feast with Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the Lord’s Supper with faith, gratitude, repentance, and love for the body. Do not treat it casually or superstitiously. Let the bread and cup lead you back to Christ’s sacrifice, call you to examine your life, and strengthen your hope until He comes.
